qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: State-granted exclusive retail electric franchise monopolies across Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Texas prevent duplicate grid infrastructure. Rate-base formula rate plans (FRPs) pass through fuel and capital costs with authorized ROEs of ~10.5-11.0%. Primary erosion risks stem from regulatory lag, severe Gulf Coast hurricane storm restoration costs, and rising cost of capital.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Inherently capital-intensive regulated electric utility failing Munger cash generation and balance sheet endurance standards: massive debt load of $27.9B against $1.77B net income (15.7x leverage vs <=4.0x threshold), thin interest coverage of 2.40x (threshold >5.0x), negative free cash flow (-$2.53B in 2025 due to $7.68B capex vs $5.15B OCF), and ongoing reliance on debt issuance and structured equity dilution to finance rate base growth.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 4.98%, structurally capped by state regulatory utility commissions (authorized ROE ~10.5-11.0%). Entergy has accelerated capital expenditures to $7.68B in 2025 (with multi-year plans exceeding $7B/yr for transmission, grid resilience, and load growth from data centers and Gulf Coast industrial facilities), significantly outstripping OCF of $5.15B and resulting in negative free cash flow. Consolidated long-term debt stands at $27.9B against $1.9B cash. EBIT of $3.20B covers interest expense of $1.34B by only 2.40x. While management has prudently de-risked the business by divesting merchant nuclear plants to focus on pure-play regulated utilities, the structural dependence on continuous capital market access violates Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency criteria.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
